metadata.title: ShadeRoute Scientific Bibliography & Institutional Citations
metadata.study_area: Bhubaneswar, Odisha (SOA ITER Campus & Surrounding 3 km²)

citations.title: Landsat 9 Thermal Infrared Sensor 2 (TIRS-2) Calibration and Surface Temperature Product Guide
citations.authors: U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) & NASA Goddard Space Flight Center
citations.venue: USGS EROS Data Center Technical Documentation Series
citations.implementation_role: Powers the high-resolution 10m microclimate Land Surface Temperature (LST) raster layer, calibrated using the Thermal Infrared Split-Window and Radiative Transfer Equations.
citations.formula_mapping: Land Surface Temperature: LST = γ · [(1/ε) · (ψ1 · L_sensor + ψ2) + ψ3] + δ
citations.apa_citation: U.S. Geological Survey & NASA. (2022). Landsat 9 Thermal Infrared Sensor 2 (TIRS-2) calibration and surface temperature product guide. USGS EROS Data Center.

citations.title: Sentinel-5 Precursor / TROPOMI Level-2 Atmospheric Products: Ozone, Nitrogen Dioxide and Aerosol Index
citations.authors: European Space Agency (ESA) & Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute (KNMI)
citations.venue: ESA Copernicus Open Access Data Documentation, S5P-KNMI-L2-0001
citations.implementation_role: Provides tropospheric ozone (O3) column densities and atmospheric aerosol optical depths to model secondary respiratory exacerbations during extreme heat.
citations.formula_mapping: Atmospheric Photochemical Stress & Secondary Respiratory Burden (J44-J45)
citations.apa_citation: European Space Agency & KNMI. (2021). Sentinel-5 Precursor / TROPOMI Level-2 atmospheric products: Ozone, nitrogen dioxide and aerosol index. ESA Copernicus Programme.

citations.title: OpenStreetMap Geodata and CARTO Voyager Cartographic Layer
citations.venue: Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODbL) & CARTO Basemaps
citations.implementation_role: Vector network geometry for campus footpaths, pedestrian walkways, building footprints, and local road transit perimeters around ITER Campus 1.
citations.formula_mapping: Pedestrian Walkway Masking & Intervention Node Allocation
citations.apa_citation: OpenStreetMap Contributors, & CARTO. (2024). OpenStreetMap vector spatial geodata and CARTO Voyager basemap. OpenStreetMap Foundation.

citations.title: The Heat Index Equation (or, More Than You Ever Wanted to Know About Heat Index)
citations.venue: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / National Weather Service Technical Attachment SR 90-23
citations.implementation_role: Mathematical multi-regression model for calculating human apparent 'Feels-Like' temperature from dry-bulb air temperature (°C) and relative humidity (%).
citations.apa_citation: Rothfusz, L. P. (1990). The heat index equation (or, more than you ever wanted to know about heat index). National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, National Weather Service Technical Attachment SR 90-23.

citations.title: Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Heat Wave Forecasting, Warning and Dissemination
citations.venue: Ministry of Earth Sciences, Government of India, New Delhi
citations.implementation_role: Establishes institutional alert criteria for Odisha: Yellow (Watch, 40°C or +4.5°C departure), Orange (Alert, >42°C for 2 consecutive days), and Red (Warning, >45°C or severe heatwave >4.5°C over normal).
citations.formula_mapping: Alert Tiers: Normal (P < 0.25), Yellow (0.25–0.50), Orange (0.50–0.70), Red (> 0.70)
citations.apa_citation: India Meteorological Department. (2023). Standard operating procedure for heat wave forecasting, warning and dissemination. Ministry of Earth Sciences, Government of India.

citations.title: Monitoring the Vernal Advancement and Retrogradation (Green Wave Effect) of Natural Vegetation
citations.authors: Rouse, J. W., Haas, R. H., Schell, J. A., & Deering, D. W.
citations.venue: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Type III Final Report, NASA-CR-139366
citations.implementation_role: Normalized Difference Vegetation Index quantifying active photosynthesizing canopy cover and tree shade deficit across all 820 micro-zones.
citations.apa_citation: Rouse, J. W., Haas, R. H., Schell, J. A., & Deering, D. W. (1974). Monitoring the vernal advancement and retrogradation (Green wave effect) of natural vegetation (NASA-CR-139366). NASA Goddard Space Flight Center.

citations.title: Use of Normalized Difference Built-up Index in Automatically Mapping Urban Areas from TM Imagery
citations.authors: Zha, Y., Gao, J., & Ni, S.
citations.implementation_role: Identifies impervious concrete walkways, building rooftops, and asphalt surfaces that act as thermal reservoirs, absorbing daytime solar radiation and re-emitting sensible heat.
citations.apa_citation: Zha, Y., Gao, J., & Ni, S. (2003). Use of normalized difference built-up index in automatically mapping urban areas from TM imagery. International Journal of Remote Sensing, 24(3), 583–594. https://doi.org/10.1080/01431160304987

citations.title: Tropical Forest Cover Density Mapping (Bare Soil Index Specification)
citations.authors: Rikimaru, A., Roy, P. S., & Miyatake, S.
citations.implementation_role: Detects unplanted bare ground and dry soil patches on campus baking under direct sun, which exhibit high ground heat and no evaporative cooling.
citations.apa_citation: Rikimaru, A., Roy, P. S., & Miyatake, S. (2002). Tropical forest cover density mapping. Tropical Ecology, 43(1), 39–47.

citations.title: NDWI—A Normalized Difference Water Index for Remote Sensing of Vegetation Liquid Water from Space
citations.implementation_role: Evaluates moisture retention and water stress in campus vegetation, determining where misting sprayers provide maximum ambient cooling benefit.
citations.apa_citation: Gao, B. C. (1996). NDWI—A normalized difference water index for remote sensing of vegetation liquid water from space. Remote Sensing of Environment, 58(3), 257–266. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0034-4257(96)00067-3

citations.authors: Harlan, S. L., Brazel, A. J., Prashad, L., Stefanov, W. L., & Larsen, L.

citations.title: Connecting People and Place: A New Framework for Reducing Urban Vulnerability to Extreme Heat
citations.authors: Wilhelmi, O. V., & Hayden, M. H.
citations.implementation_role: Guides the demographic and physical multi-criteria weighting for the Vulnerability Index (VI) across the 3 km² neighborhood catchment.

citations.title: Heat–Health Action Plans: Guidance (2nd Updated Edition)
citations.authors: World Health Organization (WHO Regional Office for Europe / Climate Change and Health)
citations.venue: WHO Guidelines Approved by the Guidelines Review Committee, Geneva, Switzerland
citations.implementation_role: Establishes tiered hospital emergency preparedness thresholds, clinical hydration stations, and the syndromic casualty influx ratios used in patient surge modeling.
citations.formula_mapping: Surge Response Tiers: Yellow (Level 1), Orange (Level 2), Red (Level 3 Emergency)
citations.apa_citation: World Health Organization. (2024). Heat–health action plans: Guidance (2nd ed.). WHO Press. https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789289071918

citations.title: National Action Plan on Heat-Related Illnesses (NAP-HRI)
citations.authors: National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
citations.venue: Government of India, Nirman Bhawan, New Delhi
citations.implementation_role: Mandates hospital Heat Stroke Units (HSUs), emergency cooling beds, ORS corners, and Integrated Health Information Platform (IHIP) heat-illness reporting standards in India.
citations.formula_mapping: HSU Bed Need (20% of excess admissions), Emergency IV Fluids (3.5L/patient)
citations.apa_citation: National Centre for Disease Control. (2024). National action plan on heat-related illnesses (NAP-HRI). Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India.

citations.title: Standard Clinical Operating Protocols for Emergency Management of Severe Heat-Related Illnesses
citations.authors: All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) Department of Emergency Medicine
citations.venue: AIIMS Emergency Medicine Clinical Review, New Delhi & Bhubaneswar
citations.implementation_role: Provides clinical guidance on cold-water immersion, active evaporative misting stations, core temperature monitoring, and ICD-10 syndromic distribution.
citations.formula_mapping: Syndromic Classification: Direct Heat (T67), Cardio (I20-I64), Renal (N17), Resp (J44)
citations.apa_citation: All India Institute of Medical Sciences. (2023). Standard clinical operating protocols for emergency management of severe heat-related illnesses. AIIMS Emergency Medicine Press.

citations.title: Ambient Temperature and Risk of Cardiovascular, Respiratory, and Metabolic Hospital Admissions: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
citations.authors: Phung, D., Thai, P. K., Guo, Y., Morawska, L., Rutherford, S., & Chu, C.
citations.implementation_role: Supplies the empirical pooled Relative Risk (RR) values per extreme heatwave event: all-cause admissions RR = 1.16, renal admissions RR = 1.30, and direct heatstroke RR = 2.45.
citations.formula_mapping: Baseline Alert Surge: β_alert = 0.35 (Pooled RR Scaling)
citations.apa_citation: Phung, D., Thai, P. K., Guo, Y., Morawska, L., Rutherford, S., & Chu, C. (2016). Ambient temperature and risk of cardiovascular, respiratory, and metabolic hospital admissions: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Environmental Research, 151, 804–814. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envres.2016.08.031
